A.explanation: Maximum amplitude positions are displacement antinodes where vigorous horizontal air motion sweeps powder away, so powder cannot settle there.

B.explanation: Piles form at displacement nodes where the air vibration amplitude is zero or minimum, so powder is undisturbed and can settle.

C.explanation: All air molecules in the stationary wave vibrate with the same frequency as the loudspeaker, so frequency cannot explain regularly spaced piles.

D.explanation: Sound in air is longitudinal so air molecules vibrate horizontally along the tube, not vertically.

hints: Notice the powder forms regularly spaced piles in the horizontal tube after the loudspeaker sets up a stationary sound wave.
Recall that a stationary wave has displacement nodes with almost no motion and antinodes with large back-and-forth motion along the wave direction.
Ask yourself where fine powder would be left undisturbed and where it would be swept away by moving air molecules.
walkthrough: Identify the set-up as a Kundt's tube: the loudspeaker wave reflects at the closed end and superposes to form a stationary longitudinal wave in air.
In a stationary wave the amplitude varies with position. Displacement nodes have minimum $0$ vibration amplitude and displacement antinodes have maximum vibration amplitude.
Sound is longitudinal, so the air molecules vibrate horizontally along the tube with the same frequency throughout.
Where the air moves vigorously at antinodes, powder is disturbed and moved away. Where the air is almost still at nodes, powder can remain and accumulate.
The regularly spaced piles therefore mark the displacement nodes of minimum amplitude. This is option B
